answer.rationale: P99 latency spiked 5x within 2 hours of a release during peak settlement write traffic. The situation mirrors b1 where a bad release caused checkout errors and rollback cleared it cleanly without customer impact. b2 warns against regional failover during hot writes—settlement traffic is currently heavy, making failover dangerous (40-minute replication gap risk). Rollback is the lowest-risk single intervention: it isolated the blast radius in b1, completed without impact, and directly addresses a release-correlated degradation. I'm verifying b1 (successful rollback pattern) and b2 (what NOT to do) to confirm rollback safety here and rule out failover. Circuit breaker (b4) protects but doesn't fix latency; read replicas (b5) help reports not writes; capacity addition requires time. Rollback removes the likely root cause in one atomic move while writes remain protected.
